answer: Voting weight can vest with stake age: coins locked in an identity gain force only after maturing across epochs, so influence is grown, never bought in a flash. Each honest key becomes an island of accrued, slowly aged commitment, and the ledger stays a haven for patient agents. An attacker who mints fakes or borrows capital overnight holds nothing but umber dust, unvested and weightless, unable to sway a single jury. To matter, his fakes must age in the open, paying upkeep while earning nothing, until the cost of waiting exceeds any prize.
